[Coach Maya]: Hi Alex, welcome. Before we begin, can you hear and see me clearly?
[Client Alex]: Yes, everything is working.
[Coach Maya]: Great. Today I’d like to understand what brought you here, clarify what success looks like, review the support available to you, and agree on your first actions. Is there anything else you want us to cover?
[Client Alex]: I want to make sure the plan is realistic with my work schedule.
[Coach Maya]: Absolutely. We’ll build that into the plan. What made you decide to get coaching now?
[Client Alex]: I’ve gained about twelve kilos over the last three years. I keep trying diets, but I stop after a few weeks.
[Coach Maya]: What usually causes you to stop?
[Client Alex]: Work becomes stressful. I skip workouts, order food, and then feel like I’ve failed.
[Coach Maya]: So the recurring pattern is stress, missed routines, convenience food, and then an all-or-nothing reaction. Does that feel accurate?
[Client Alex]: Yes, exactly.
[Coach Maya]: What would you most like to change over the next six months?
[Client Alex]: I’d like to lose eight to ten kilos, improve my energy, and feel comfortable in my clothes again.
[Coach Maya]: Beyond the number on the scale, why does that matter to you?
[Client Alex]: I want to be active with my children. Right now I avoid playing football with them because I get tired quickly.
[Coach Maya]: Being energetic and present with your children sounds like the bigger reason behind the goal.
[Client Alex]: Yes. That matters more than just looking different.
[Coach Maya]: If nothing changed during the next year, what would concern you most?
[Client Alex]: My health getting worse and my children seeing me treat exercise as something unpleasant.
[Coach Maya]: Let’s use being an active role model for your children as your North Star. We can return to it when motivation is low. Does that language work for you?
[Client Alex]: It does.
[Coach Maya]: Walk me through a typical weekday, starting with sleep.
[Client Alex]: I sleep around six hours. I usually skip breakfast, eat something quick at my desk, and have a large dinner. I exercise maybe once a week.
[Coach Maya]: How many days per week do you currently drink alcohol?
[Client Alex]: Usually Friday and Saturday, around three drinks each time.
[Coach Maya]: Are there any injuries, medical conditions, medications, or movements that affect your ability to train?
[Client Alex]: No medical conditions or medications. My right knee sometimes feels stiff, but it has not been diagnosed as an injury.
[Coach Maya]: Thank you. Please stop and seek medical guidance if the knee becomes painful. We’ll begin with low-impact options and monitor it rather than diagnosing it ourselves.
[Client Alex]: That sounds sensible.
[Coach Maya]: On a scale from one to ten, how confident are you that you can complete two thirty-minute sessions next week?
[Client Alex]: About an eight.
[Coach Maya]: What makes it an eight rather than a five?
[Client Alex]: Two sessions feel manageable, and I can do them before work.
[Coach Maya]: What could prevent them from happening?
[Client Alex]: A late night at work or sleeping through my alarm.
[Coach Maya]: How could we make the plan more resilient?
[Client Alex]: I could schedule Tuesday and Thursday mornings, with Saturday as a backup.
[Coach Maya]: Excellent. Let’s make that specific: Tuesday and Thursday at 7:00 a.m., with Saturday at 10:00 a.m. as the backup. Will you add those to your calendar today?
[Client Alex]: Yes, I’ll add them immediately after this call.
[Coach Maya]: For nutrition, I don’t want you to overhaul everything at once. Which single change would have the greatest impact this week?
[Client Alex]: Preparing lunch instead of ordering food.
[Coach Maya]: How many lunches can you realistically prepare?
[Client Alex]: Three—Monday, Wednesday, and Thursday.
[Coach Maya]: What will you prepare, and when will you shop?
[Client Alex]: Chicken or tofu with rice and vegetables. I’ll shop Sunday morning and prepare the meals Sunday afternoon.
[Coach Maya]: Great. Your actions are two scheduled workouts and three prepared lunches. My action is to send you the beginner low-impact session and the meal-building guide by 5:00 p.m. today.
[Client Alex]: Perfect.
[Coach Maya]: We’ll track completed workouts, prepared lunches, average sleep, and a weekly weight trend. Weight is information, not a judgment. Are you comfortable tracking those?
[Client Alex]: Yes.
[Coach Maya]: If you miss one action, what will you do instead of abandoning the week?
[Client Alex]: Use the backup workout slot or prepare the next meal rather than waiting for Monday.
[Coach Maya]: Exactly. We’re aiming for consistency, not perfection. How would you like me to hold you accountable?
[Client Alex]: A short message on Friday would help.
[Coach Maya]: I’ll message you Friday afternoon and ask specifically about the two workouts and three lunches.
[Client Alex]: Great.
[Coach Maya]: Let’s book our next call now. I have Tuesday, September 8 at 6:00 p.m. or Wednesday, September 9 at 7:00 p.m.
[Client Alex]: Tuesday, September 8 at 6:00 p.m. works.
[Coach Maya]: Confirmed—I’ve booked Tuesday, September 8 at 6:00 p.m. and sent the calendar invitation. Can you see it?
[Client Alex]: Yes, I’ve received and accepted it.
[Coach Maya]: Before we finish, can you summarize your commitments in your own words?
[Client Alex]: I’ll add the workouts to my calendar today, train Tuesday and Thursday at 7:00 a.m. with Saturday as backup, shop Sunday morning, and prepare three lunches Sunday afternoon.
[Coach Maya]: And I’ll send the workout and meal guide by 5:00 p.m. today, then check in Friday afternoon. What questions or concerns are still unresolved?
[Client Alex]: None. I’m clear on what to do.
[Coach Maya]: How confident do you feel about the plan now?
[Client Alex]: Nine out of ten. It feels specific without being overwhelming.
[Coach Maya]: Excellent. Your goal this week is to collect evidence that you can follow a realistic plan, not to be perfect. I’ll speak with you on September 8.
[Client Alex]: Thank you. I’m ready to start.
